title: The best robot vacuum and mop deals during October Prime Day

The Dreame X60 Ultra in action. | Photo by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge	

Spending too much time constantly sweeping and mopping? If you have the money to delegate those chores to a robot cleaner, you could save a lot of personal time. Thankfully, it’s cheaper than usual to buy a robot vacuum / mop hybrid during Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days, and some of our favorite models are discounted. The deals aren’t just for Amazon Prime members either, with other retailers like Best Buy and manufacturers getting in on the action, as well. 
That being said, if your floors are already squeaky clean, make sure to check out our roundup of over 100 deals from Amazon’s October sale.

title: Amazon’s last-gen Kindle Paperwhite is 30 percent off
summary: The 2024 Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is discounted 30 percent to $169.99, offering excellent value with 300ppi display, waterproofing, and wireless charging despite minor performance differences from the newest model. The discount makes it an attractive option for budget-conscious e-reader buyers.
content:
Calling something “last-gen” usually means it comes with big compromises compared to the latest version. That’s not as true for the last-gen Kindle Paperwhite as it is with some other tech. The newer version can open books 30 percent faster (not the same as page-turning speed), and its aluminum design is a millimeter thinner — but it costs $50 more.
The 2024 edition has the same fantastic 300ppi screen, an auto-adjusting front light, and waterproof (IPX8) design. And the Signature Edition that’s discounted has no lockscreen ads, twice the storage (32GB) of the base model, plus wireless charging and an ambient light sensor, and it’s down to $169.99 (originally $249.99) at Amazon.
Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition
The premium Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition offers the same design and performance as the standard model but with more storage and support for wireless charging.

Where to Buy:

 $249.99 $169.99 at Amazon
 $249.99 $169.99 at Best Buy
 $249.99 $169.99 at Target

The standard Paperwhite is $149.99 (was $199.99) at Amazon, and while the lower price is nice, I’d suggest only opting for that model if you’re alright with what you’re giving up (which is a lot): it has half the storage, no wireless charging, and lockscreen ads.

title: The easiest Apple Watch to recommend is $50 off

content:
The discounted Apple Watch SE 3. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge	

The Apple Watch SE 3 is the smartwatch that we recommend for most people because it’s affordable, yet packed with most of the features found in pricier versions. We spotted Amazon October Prime Day discounts across the lineup, including both the 40mm and 44mm sizes, and GPS only or cellular options. The Wi-Fi and GPS model is $199 for the 40mm size (matching the lowest price to date), and $229 for the 44m size. If you also want a cellular connection, the 40mm version is $249, and the 44mm version is $279.
Apple Watch SE 3
The Apple Watch SE 3 is a major glow-up, adding an always-on display, wrist-temperature sensor, a more powerful processor, and fast charging. Read our review.

 $249 $199 at Amazon

title: The planetary wave headed for California isn’t what you think it is
summary: A Kelvin wave bringing warm water from the Pacific is moving toward California and raising sea levels along already vulnerable coasts. While not a 'freak' phenomenon—such waves occur regularly—this particular one could have more dramatic consequences than typical events.
content:
An aerial view of equipment moving fresh sand during an emergency replenishment project along eroding shoreline at North Beach on August 15th, 2024, in San Clemente, California. | Photo: Getty Images	

A rather strong "planetary wave" recently slammed into South America and is making its way toward California. In case you're worried about headlines warning of the supposedly "freak" phenomenon "bringing trouble," it's worth understanding what this wave really is and isn't.
Called a Kelvin wave, it's carrying warm water to the Americas that's typically trapped farther west. That's raising sea levels along already vulnerable coastlines. These kinds of waves are common. When they do arrive, they can exacerbate existing problems. And this particular Kelvin wave could have more dramatic consequences than usual.

During Amazon’s October sale, the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL are discounted by $250 or more. The base model Pixel 11 Pro with 256GB of storage is only $849 (originally $1,099), $50 lower than the usual price for the base Pixel 11, while the 256GB 11 Pro XL is $999, a $300 price break. 
Even the regular Pixel 11 with 256GB of storage is cheaper, selling at $749, $150 off the normal price. But with the Pro at just a $100 premium over the Pixel 11 right now instead of $200, its superior cameras alone is a pretty convincing reason to spend more.
Google Pixel 11 Pro

Where to Buy:

 $1099 $849 at Amazon

We praised the Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL for their new camera modes, as well as the Magic Capture mode. We liked some of the Gemini-assisted features, like Rambler for smoothing out voice texting, but others, like proactive assistance, felt a bit more narrow.

title: The best October Prime Day tech deals we found
summary: The Verge has curated the top tech deals from Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days event, featuring significant discounts on phones, laptops, and accessories through October 8. Notable offers include the iPhone Air at $839.99, Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra at $979.99, and MacBook Air M5 with $200 off.
content:
Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days event has begun, and it lasts through 3AM ET on Thursday, October 8th. We’ve spun through the company’s huge list of deals to find products that Verge readers will like (and that we personally like, too). Prime subscribers can get in on plenty of headphone deals, plus some great products in the home entertainment space. Also, the discounts are spectacular on Pixel 11 phones, the A17 Pro-equipped iPad Mini, and the M5 MacBook Air. 
We’re changing up how we’re presenting the deals. Usually, these posts are huge and require a lot of scrolling, but we wanted to make it easier to find what you’re looking for. All of the deals are in a table that you can sort by category.
We’ll add more deals as we find them, and we’ll also include links to various category-specific roundups we’ll be publishing throughout the sale.
iPhone Air
The iPhone Air is Apple’s thinnest iPhone yet at 5.6mm, featuring a 6.5-inch ProMotion display, a 48MP fusion camera, and an 18MP front camera with Center Stage support. But its single rear camera and “meh” battery life mean it’s not for everyone.

Where to Buy:

 $999.99 $839.99 at Best Buy (256GB)

iPhone 16E
The iPhone 16E is the spiritual successor to the iPhone SE, bringing flagship-level performance for less than the standard 16. We really wish it included MagSafe for $599, but those upgrading from older iPhones will probably be satisfied with what’s included.

Where to Buy:

 $599.99 $489.99 at Best Buy (128GB)

Belkin Charging Case Pro
While it won’t charge your Switch 2 any faster than the cheaper Belkin option, the clever battery-meets-kickstand with a built-in display simply looks better.

Where to Buy:

 $99.99 $80.74 at Amazon (sand)
 $99.99 $84.99 at Belkin (sand)

Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra
Samsung recently increased the price of all its S26 phones, but you can get the best of the bunch, the S26 Ultra, at one of its best prices of the year. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $1299.99 $979.99 at Amazon (256GB)

title: Amazon Alexa Plus keeps creepily singing ‘lalala’ for minutes on end
summary: Multiple Amazon Echo smart home speakers running Alexa Plus have been affected by a bug causing them to repeatedly sing or say "lalala" for extended periods. The issue has been reported across multiple Echo models and Amazon acknowledges awareness of the problem.
content:
The Amazon Echo Studio is one of the speakers that runs Alexa Plus. | Photo by John Higgins / The Verge	

An unsettling Alexa Plus bug has seen some Amazon Echo smart home speakers reduced to saying - and sometimes singing - nothing but "lalala" on repeat for minutes at a time, often in the middle of conversations with users. When quizzed about the behavior, Alexa is apparently entirely unaware of what it's been doing.
The issue has been reported on Reddit repeatedly over the last few weeks, as recently as three days ago, across multiple types of Echo speaker. Multiple users have uploaded videos of the speakers' strange behavior. Here's one that Android Authority uploaded to YouTube:

title: This remote-controlled wagon is silly but so very useful
summary: BougeRV's remote-controlled DuneRover wagon, while unconventional with animated lighting, proves surprisingly capable with enough torque to traverse challenging terrain and carry over 200 pounds of gear. Production units are expected to ship in February 2027.
content:
Confession: When BougeRV told me about its remote-controlled wagon with animated lighting, I called it in for a laugh, expecting to eviscerate it in a review. It's ridiculous, to be sure. But the DuneRover also proved very capable, with enough torque to flatten hills even when carrying over 200 pounds of gear. It can also traverse soft sand that defeats conventional wagons. 
As someone who regularly uses a variety of wagons to haul all sorts of gear, the DuneRover is an epiphany. But what BougeRV sent me was a Kickstarter prototype - and it shows.
